After excimer laser keratective surgery, both advanced surface ablation and sub-Bowman's keratomileusis (SBK) have been shown to maintain corneal biomechanics. However, there is evidence suggesting that SBK may be more effective in reducing the risk of corneal haze.

Advanced surface ablation involves removing the epithelial layer and deepening the stromal layer without significantly increasing the thickness of the epithelium. This technique has been shown to promote wound healing by creating a physical barrier between the epithelial cells and the underlying collagen fibers, which helps to maintain corneal structure and function.

Sub-Bowman's keratomileusis, on the other hand, involves removing a specific layer of the cornea beneath Bowman's hyalinized tissue. This technique has been shown to be effective in promoting wound healing by creating a physical barrier between the epithelial cells and the underlying collagen fibers, which helps to maintain corneal structure and function.

Studies have found that patients who undergo SBK tend to have better outcomes in terms of maintaining corneal biomechanics compared to those who undergo advanced surface ablation. Additionally, SBK may be associated with a lower risk of corneal haze.

However, it is essential to note that both techniques have their own set of complications and limitations. Advanced surface ablation carries the risk of epithelial complications, including dry eye syndrome, while sub-Bowman's keratomileusis carries the risk of posterior capsular opacification (PCO).

In conclusion, both advanced surface ablation and SBK are effective techniques for promoting wound healing after excimer laser keratective surgery, but they may have different biomechanical and wound healing characteristics. Further studies are needed to fully understand the differences between these two techniques and their potential impact on patient outcomes.

It is essential to discuss individual patient needs and risks with a qualified healthcare professional before undergoing any type of eye surgery.
